chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abi Nasr, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), who said:
The perfume (or pleasant scent) is from the etiquettes of the Prophets.
ai.seo_question: What is the religious significance of using perfume in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the use of perfume is elevated from mere hygiene to a defining moral characteristic (akhlaq) of the Prophets, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the harmony between physical purity and spiritual nobility. This tradition is often contextualized within the broader Prophetic practice of using musk and saffron, serving as a reminder that outward beauty should mirror inner virtue. It encourages believers to cultivate a pleasant presence as an act of worship and social etiquette, rooted in the exemplary conduct of the Ahl al-Bayt.
